# Summary

Adds **W8A8 MXFP8** quantization (8-bit weights + 8-bit activations, block_size = 32) for Qwen3 / Qwen3.5 **MoE** (FusedMoE) LLM models on Ascend NPU, continuing the NPU quantization work tracked in #21584. Both **online** (`--quantization mxfp8`) and **offline** (msmodelslim, flagless — selected by the checkpoint's `quant_model_description.json`) paths are supported and share the same fused-experts kernel. Requires Ascend A5 (Ascend 950) — the fused MoE MX kernels (`npu_grouped_matmul_swiglu_quant_v2`, `npu_dynamic_mx_quant`) are A5-only.

> #23795 (dense W4A4) has landed and this branch is merged up to `main`, so the diff is now the MoE MXFP8 delta only. It reuses the merged dense MXFP8 infrastructure — `NPUMXFP8LinearMethod`, the `Fp8Config` NPU dispatch, and `ModelSlimMXFP8Scheme` (from #22352).

**Online quantization (`--quantization mxfp8`)**

- On the **Ascend NPU** backend, `Fp8Config.get_quant_method()` dispatches FusedMoE layers to the new `NPUMXFP8OnlineMoEMethod` (the `isinstance(layer, FusedMoE)` branch, mirroring the existing dense `NPUMXFP8LinearMethod` linear branch). It subclasses `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod` and overrides only `create_moe_runner`, to attach the MXFP8 per-gmm kernels — weight creation, weight post-processing and the forward pass are the unquantized Ascend ones. On GPU the `FusedMoE` branch is untouched.
- BF16/FP16 expert weights `w13`/`w2` are quantised once at load via `npu_dynamic_mx_quant(dst_type = torch_npu.float8_e4m3fn)` — a 3D `[E, N, K]` input is accepted directly (no per-expert loop) — into `float8_e4m3fn` weights + UE8M0 (`float8_e8m0fnu`) block scales, kept as **non-contiguous transpose views**.
- Forward: on the `ascend_tp` dispatcher, `npu_moe_init_routing_v2` with **`quant_mode=3`** (count `group_list`) — the per-token MXFP8 activation quant is fused directly into routing, so the same kernel launch emits the sorted `float8_e4m3fn` payload *and* its `float8_e8m0fnu` block scale, saving a separate `npu_dynamic_mx_quant` pass — → **gmm1** `npu_grouped_matmul_swiglu_quant_v2` (gate_up + swiglu + requant fused, **cumulative** `group_list`) → **gmm2** `npu_grouped_matmul` (**count** `group_list` + explicit `group_list_type`). The UE8M0 scale dtypes are passed explicitly; the e4m3 `x`/`weight` dtypes are left implicit. DeepEP has no MXFP8 dispatch dtype, so on that path the dispatcher keeps sending BF16 and gmm1 quantizes the hidden states itself via `npu_dynamic_mx_quant` before the fused kernel — both dispatchers reach gmm1 with the same input. Only the `ascend_tp` path is validated end-to-end on A5.
- **Fused-routing quant optimization:** the fused `quant_mode=3` scale comes back flat (`[N, K/32]`) instead of the pair-split `[N, K/64, 2]` layout gmm1 expects, so `_normalize_mxfp_scale` reshapes it before use. Part 3 of the 3-PR stack (base: #33012). RFC: #30696. Re-lands the reader migration reverted in #32100, regenerated from scratch against current main with the revert's defects fixed at their origin.

- Mechanical sweep (AST-based, alias-aware): `get_server_args().FIELD` / `self.server_args.FIELD` / local-alias reads flip to the namespace accessors (`get_exec()` / `get_memory()` / …), routed by each field's NS metadata — 628 reads across 160 files.
- Kept by rule, not omission: parallel-namespace leaves (their own follow-up), per-runner fork fields (attention backends / context_length / load_format / skip_tokenizer_init / kv_cache_dtype — the draft worker's private copy rewrites these, so resolved values belong to the runner), per-instance manager files (tokenizer family and multimodal processors: with several engines in one process their reads must stay on `self.server_args`), the resolution pipeline, construction-boundary files, and parameter-form reads.
- `declare_load_time_override` now writes the config bags via `get_context().override` (namespace readers see the declaration immediately); `server_args` stays the pristine startup record. During a draft build the declaration lands on — and is discarded with — the draft's own bags.
- kv-cache dtype: the `get_model().kv_cache_dtype` bag leaf now always holds the RAW user intent. ## Summary

Applies the `ShortConvAttnBackend` sidecar from #29867 to **Inkling**, and fixes the 4x redundant per-step metadata prep that motivated it.

`ShortConvolution` no longer touches the pool. It reads a per-(layer, step) handle from `get_attn_backend().conv_state_metadata()`, and the new `InklingShortConvAttnBackend` owns the step-global conv metadata:

- the per-request slot gather + virtual->physical translate
- the fused `query_start_loc` / `has_initial_state` / `(cache_mask, safe_idx, cu, si)` launch
- the extend prefix-cache `track_conv_indices`

**The 4x.** Ownership used to be keyed on `layer_id == 0`, but an Inkling decoder layer holds FOUR `ShortConvolution` modules (`k_sconv`, `v_sconv`, `attn_sconv`, `mlp_sconv`), so each of those three preps ran four times per step instead of once. Profiled decode step: **3342 vs 3561 kernels**, with `_fused_decode_metadata_kernel` 7 vs 28 and `_fused_extend_metadata_kernel` 5 vs 20 (4x -> 1x).

The second commit finishes the job: the accepted-verify conv commit moves off the model into the backend, removing Inkling's last model-side pool access.

## Hook placement is a perf cliff, not a style choice

Metadata prep belongs in `init_forward_metadata_in_graph`, which the decode / target-verify / draft-extend runners **record** into the graph so it replays for free. Resolving it in `init_forward_metadata_out_graph` instead **measured ~7% off decode throughput** -- a captured graph is precisely where per-step CPU launches hurt. `_out_graph` now takes only what a phase cannot record: the full-cuda-graph prefill (whose runner has no in-graph hook) and, for the unified memory pool, the slot translate.

Because prep no longer sits in the model it no longer sits in the graph, so every tensor a captured conv kernel reads lives in a graph-static buffer refilled in place -- the same contract as `ShortConvAttnBackend._cache_indices_buf` and the full-attention backend's `swa_out_cache_loc_buf`.

## Bugs found by GPU e2e

- **`_alloc_cache_indices_buf` reallocated on `init_cuda_graph_state`**, which the decode runner calls *after* the prefill graphs already captured the address -> illegal memory access. Now grow-only with an assert. Signature: each graph phase alone passes, both together fail.
- **The padded tail of the track-index buffer must be zeroed, not left stale.** The old in-graph build clamped the whole padded range to this batch's token count, so stale rows index outside the current token buffer.
- **`DraftBackendFactory` bypasses `attn_backend_wrapper`.** Right for mamba hybrids (their MTP draft has no linear layers -- the same premise behind the base wrapper's DRAFT_EXTEND_V2 skip), but Inkling's MTP draft ships its own `model.mtp.layers.*.k_sconv` / `v_sconv`, so it needs the sidecar too. Added `attn_backend_wrapper_for_draft_extend`, Inkling-only and a no-op elsewhere.
- **Wrapping hijacked the MTP-verify commit.** The spec workers dispatch on `hasattr(attn_backend, "update_mamba_state_after_mtp_verify")`, so inheriting the generic mamba scatter routed Inkling's six per-stream conv caches into it (`indices length mismatch: dst=15 vs step=16`). The generic version sources slot ids from `forward_metadata`, which is stale by the time the commit runs -- it happens after the forward context exits. Fixed by giving the hook `req_pool_indices` and implementing the commit on Inkling's backend.

json.body: ## Purpose Add **VidCom2** (Video Compression Commander) as a second training-free video token pruning method alongside EVS, enabled via `--video-retention-ratio`. - Paper: Liu et al., *"Video Compression Commander: Plug-and-Play Inference Acceleration for Video Large Language Models"*, EMNLP 2025 — - Reference implementation (Apache-2.0): Unlike EVS (temporal dissimilarity to the previous frame, first frame always fully retained), VidCom2 scores tokens by multi-scale Gaussian similarity to video-level and frame-level feature centers over the lowest-variance channels, and allocates a **dynamic per-frame budget** (softmax over frame-level distinctiveness) so distinctive frames keep more tokens. This follows the authors' released reference implementation, which is what produced the published accuracy numbers. ### Changes - `vllm/multimodal/vidcom2.py` — new module with `compute_retained_tokens_count` / `compute_retention_mask`, mirroring the EVS module's contract. Adds an exact-count reconcile step so the mask total always equals the placeholder count computed at prompt-processing time (vLLM sizes placeholders before the mask exists). - `MultiModalConfig.video_retention_ratio` (range `(0;1]`, mutually exclusive with `video_pruning_rate`, validated) + `get_video_pruning_spec()` returning a unified `(method, q)` tuple so downstream code stays method-agnostic. - `--video-retention-ratio` engine arg. - Qwen3-VL (dense + MoE via inheritance): placeholder sizing and retention-mask computation route through the selected method; the EVS path is unchanged when `--video-pruning-rate` is used. - `SupportsMultiModalPruning.supported_video_pruning_methods` ClassVar (default `("evs",)`; Qwen3-VL overrides with `("evs", "vidcom2")`) with a fail-fast check at model-load time, so EVS-only models (Qwen2.5-VL, InternS1-Pro, Nano-Nemotron-VL, …) reject `--video-retention-ratio` with a clear startup error instead of crashing mid-forward with `q=None`. ### Licensing / attribution The scoring in `vllm/multimodal/vidcom2.py` is adapted from the authors' Apache-2.0 reference implementation; the file header carries an "Adapted from" notice with the repo URL, copyright line, and paper citation. ### Non-duplication Searched issues and open PRs for `vidcom`, `2505.14454`, and "video compression commander": no existing or in-flight VidCom2 work in this repo. The closest related feature is EVS (#29752), which this PR extends rather than duplicates. ## Test Plan ```bash # Unit tests (CPU-only, no GPU required) pytest tests/multimodal/test_vidcom2.py -v # Lint pre-commit run --files vllm/multimodal/vidcom2.py vllm/config/multimodal.py \ vllm/config/model.py vllm/engine/arg_utils.py \ vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_vl.py \ vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py tests/multimodal/test_vidcom2.py \ docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md docs/design/cuda_graphs_multimodal.md # E2E (GPU) vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct --video-retention-ratio 0.25 ``` ## Test Result All tests and lints passed. ### Quality Vidcom consistently outperforms EVS on the same normalized pruning rate (i.e. for vidcom = 1- retentionrate). Tested on 500 MCQ on a single H100 (Cosmos Reason 2 8B). ### Performance TTFT is equal to EVS. Requests: 50, OSL: 500, ISL: 86 This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude). ## Motivation

The `.claude/skills/sglang-runtime-context` skill still described the retired resolve-at-end contract (a single resolved `ServerArgs` as the source of truth, `ServerArgs.override` as the mutation entry) — actively misleading for anyone touching config now.

Rewrite the config sections for the landed model and the two units below this PR:

- `ServerArgs` is a pristine published seed; resolved config lives in the namespace bags, projected at `publish(server_args, role=...)` per process entry; per-role enforcement modes documented.
- Post-publish mutation goes through `get_context().override` (bag-only); `ServerArgs.override` is being retired behind the writer ratchet, and rerouting a writer co-flips all its readers in the same commit.
- Documented the reads that legitimately stay on an instance (per-runner fork fields, per-instance tokenizer/entrypoints boundaries, whole-object passes), `get_parallel()`'s config/live dual semantics with the live-shadowed sizes rule, `preserve_config` for nested publishes, and the bag-only `declare_load_time_override` route.
- Testing idioms: publish-seeding instead of faking accessors or SimpleNamespace stand-ins; per-file test runs to avoid leaked-publish masking.

Symmetric-memory allocations are per-forward, so an address taken from that pool during graph capture is neither reserved for the graph's lifetime nor at the same offset on every rank. Under capture this corrupts DSPARK speculative decoding: accept collapses to 1.000, or (worse) the server silently emits garbage while reporting accept pinned at the ceiling, with no error. The flag is now forced off on Kimi hybrid archs unless every phase runs eager; the auto-probed K3 fused all-reduce is faster than the symm-mem path anyway.

## Motivation

Both attention backends assume a uniform query head count across layers. Models that set `num_attention_heads_per_layer` (e.g. `poolside/Laguna-S-2.1`, 48–72 heads) break:

## What this does

Extends `--enable-unified-memory` to **MLA-hybrid-Mamba** models (Kimi-Linear), on the Triton attention backend.

Unified memory replaces the two static pools — a full-KV pool and a Mamba/linear-attention state pool, split once at startup by `--mamba-full-memory-ratio` and never rebalanced — with a single shared buffer that two `MultiEndedAllocator`s grow into from opposite ends. The pain it removes is one side idling while the other retracts or OOMs. The MHA-hybrid version already landed upstream; this adds the MLA-hybrid case.

## Design: dense views

The MLA layers have uniform entries (`kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim` = 576 wide for Kimi-Linear), and the page-major envelope is already a legal dense paged pool — so no new physical layout is needed, only index renumbering:

- each layer gets a contiguous view into the envelope starting at byte `l · page_size · E` (`build_dense_mla_views`)

When using speculative decoding (MTP) with Quark-quantized MoE models (e.g. `amd/DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4`), the vLLM server crashes during model loading with:

vLLM loads the speculative decoding draft model as a separate module with its own MoE layers. Quark's `get_quant_method()` uses **name-based pattern matching** on layer prefixes to determine the quantization method. Hybrid (mamba) models previously asserted out heterogeneous block sizes entirely — yet they are the models where P/D block sizes most readily diverge, since the mamba-padded attention block size varies with TP sharding (#41037). Lift the restriction:

- Mamba state blocks are indivisible, so their descriptors always use local page geometry and their desc ids are never ratio-expanded; attention descriptors remain expanded to remote-block granularity.

- The receive post-process permutes only attention-layer caches (a lazily cached list) and zeroes everything past the transferred coverage — the untransferred token tail of the last partially covered block plus any blocks beyond it — whose zeroing the scheduler skipped for the load. The clip happens at remote-block granularity with a block-size ratio, and at kernel-block granularity when equal kernel pages meet differing logical block sizes, so mamba hybrids need this zeroing even when the ratio is 1 (including MLA).

`InputBatch.make_dummy` and `GPUModelRunner._dummy_run` gave every dummy request `num_tokens // num_reqs` tokens and dumped the entire remainder on the last request, so a single dummy request could have `seq_len = query_len` up to `num_tokens - num_reqs + 1` tokens, far exceeding `max_model_len`. Such a request cannot be backed by the block tables (width `cdiv(max_model_len, block_size)`, alignment-padded): any attention kernel that runs on the dummy batch walks block-table entries past the end of the tensor and consumes garbage page IDs.

This is what broke CI when #49364 made piecewise cudagraph capture build attn metadata and run attention eagerly on the dummy batch: for capture size 496 with `max_num_seqs=256` and max_model_len=16, the last dummy request had 241 tokens (16 KV pages vs an 8-slot block-table row). FA3's paged mainloop `read block_table[255][8..15]` out of bounds and prefetched K/V at garbage page addresses - an illegal memory access whenever those landed on unmapped memory (reliably fatal on the 16GB MIG CI runner, silent on larger GPUs), which is why #49364 had to be reverted (#49451).

Distribute the remainder evenly instead (the first `num_tokens % num_reqs` requests get one extra token), so every dummy request has at most `ceil(num_tokens / num_reqs) <= max_model_len` tokens and the dummy batch is valid by construction. With this, #49364 can be re-landed unchanged.

Hybrid/Mamba models support an align-mode Mamba cache path where the running Mamba state is migrated at scheduler-step / block boundaries. Hybrid (mamba) models previously asserted out heterogeneous block sizes entirely — yet they are the models where P/D block sizes most readily diverge, since the mamba-padded attention block size varies with TP sharding (#41037). Lift the restriction:

- Mamba state blocks are indivisible, so their descriptors always use local page geometry and their desc ids are never ratio-expanded; attention descriptors remain expanded to remote-block granularity.
- A shared per-group mapping (pull READ and push WRITE) expands attention groups to remote granularity and clips to the transferred coverage, while mamba groups map 1:1.
- The receive post-process permutes only attention-layer caches (a lazily cached list) and zeroes everything past the transferred coverage — the untransferred token tail of the last partially covered block plus any blocks beyond it — whose zeroing the scheduler skipped for the load. The clip happens at remote-block granularity with a block-size ratio, and at kernel-block granularity when equal kernel pages meet differing logical block sizes, so mamba hybrids need this zeroing even when the ratio is 1 (including MLA).
- The multi-read hetero-TP path (P_TP > D_TP with sharded SSM state, #49297) builds its per-source split handles from the remote- granularity descriptors, keyed by (tp_ratio, remote_block_size); replicated and single-source attention descriptors pass through whole, and SSM chunking is unaffected by the ratio.

## Purpose

see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45702

Enable fine-grained prefix lookup and MooncakeStore offload when a prompt ends before the shared block boundary. Handle lazy hash sequences and local-only partial hits correctly so sub-block requests can reuse cached state without triggering an invalid remote load.

### `max_tokens=1` failure mode

A producer's partial-tail marker previously became an offload handoff only when a later allocation triggered copy-on-write. Requests that finished after their first sample never allocated again, so freeing the request discarded the marker and forced later consumers to recompute that otherwise shareable tail. As a result, the tail was not offloaded when `max_tokens=1`.

Flush partial-tail handoffs in the scheduling step that creates them, carry the exact snapshot boundary, and pin off-table Mamba CoW blocks until connector-delayed free completes. Persist every cache group from its durable offset through the boundary, including smaller-group full blocks that normal LCM-aligned saves omit.

Gate producer-only work on connector availability and fail closed under pressure, null source blocks, lookup errors, or failed puts. Keep partial-tail progress separate from normal-save progress so failed offloads remain cache misses instead of publishing corrupt data or advancing the durable watermark.
